title: add_packet_field should return value and offset
description:
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/migration-test/-/issues/13033

Summary of the original issue:

The lua function add_packet_field() additionally returns the parsed value in some cases and not others. The documentation promises a return value in all cases. It is cumbersome to declare and then call a separate Field object to access data when your own code is doing the analysis. It should be possible to add a value to the tree and also make that value accessible to your code with a single call.

This is a draft in order to validate the overall approach before continuing work.

1. Use existing functions in proto.c such as proto_tree_add_item_ret_int to get a proper return values.

2. If there is no corresponding function in proto.c, then write one e.g. proto_tree_add_item_ret_float()

3. Create a new file in the test suite focusing on validating the return values for lua. The return values from add_packet_field() should be the same values you get from calling the corresponding methods directly on the tvbrange, e.g. tvbrange:int().

~~Perhaps: There is an undocumented third return containing the offset after the parsed data. Implement, document, and test this offset as well.~~ The third return is implemented and documented.

The implementation covers field types except:

ipxnet, framenum, guid, and eui64

These aren't covered because they aren't well supported in the Lua API generally.

notes.body:
Just a small issue. I would avoid changing the behavior of an already existing method. It could break existing behavior, especially for a method like this. Would it make more sense, to better document the current behavior and create a new method for the improved behavior?

If we change the method itself, we would also need to update the release notes in doc/. Actually changing it now, would at least put the change in the new upcoming version, which might become a major update (aka 4.0) and would allow breaking changes.

We already have tree_item:add and tree_item:add_packet_field. In addition to returning more useful values, a new method could improve upon add_packet_field by making the encoding parameter optional, defaulting big-endian.
